abstract:
Complex fields such as bioinformatics and artificial intelligence (AI) in medicine depend on big data and advanced computational tools. Consequently, they require structured platforms that enable collaborative development and academic capabilities. This report aims to demonstrate the pedagogical value of a version control system in an academic setting by deploying a dedicated local server for teaching AI in the field of medical sciences and developing bioinformatics software tools.
We implemented a web-based, self-hosted platform for managing educational courses and developing AI-driven bioinformatics tools. This platform is based on the Git ecosystem as a decentralized version control system which facilitates collaboration among distributed teams.
The implemented platform enables comprehensive repository management and secure user access control, providing an integrated collaborative environment. It also supports educational activities, including course definition, sharing of teaching materials, and assignment submission. Within this framework, students and instructors can effectively coordinate tasks and store detailed project documentation throughout all stages of tool development. As a practical example, a new bioinformatics software package was successfully developed using this platform, demonstrating the system's effectiveness in supporting both educational and research-oriented software development.
Our platform provides a secure and scalable environment for teaching and research in bioinformatics and AI in medicine. It provides advanced collaboration features that support learning activities and the development of computational tools, essential for improving both educational and research outcomes. We recommend its use in academic and research settings to strengthen the required skills and practices for advances in medicine and biology.
